transcript.text: I think my washer dryer has a fault - I put it on just a drying programme with dry-ish clothes and I can hear water running into it and draining the whole time. Surely it shouldn't use water to dry? It's a Beko.

It sounds like your Beko washer-dryer is behaving normally for a condensing model. Most washer-dryers use a trickle of cold water during the drying cycle to cool down the hot, moist air so it can condense into liquid and be pumped away. If you hear running water and draining, that is likely the condensation process working. However, if there is excessive leaking or the clothes are soaking wet afterwards, we need to rule out a blockage. Could you please switch the machine off and unplug it? Then check the pump filter (usually behind a small flap at the bottom front) and tell me if it was full of fluff or debris. Also, is there any water leaking from that area onto the floor?

Thank you. There's no leak on the floor and the clothes come out perfectly dry, so nothing is actually wrong as such. I haven't checked the pump filter yet - is that really necessary if it's working properly?

[Heading: Normal condensing operation]
You are quite right to question it, but your machine is behaving normally. Beko washer-dryers (and most condenser models) use a small trickle of cold water during the drying cycle to cool down the hot, moist air so it turns back into liquid and can be pumped away. Since your clothes come out dry and there are no leaks, this process is working exactly as designed. Regarding the pump filter: while it isn't strictly necessary if everything is running perfectly right now, I would strongly recommend checking it once or twice a year. Drying generates fluff that goes down the drain path; clearing it prevents future blockages and keeps the drying efficient. If you ever notice longer drying times or water backing up later on, that will be your first clue to clean it.

candidates.cause: Normal condensation process (cold water supply active)
Blocked pump filter or drain hose causing backup/leakage noise
Faulty water inlet valve leaking continuously
